cards.title: Tidepool Timekeepers Lab
cards.useCase: Adult-led, offline, paper-only printable story map card for arranging pretend tidepool lab moments from first clue to final change: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Print one card, set out pencils, and ask the writer to invent a tiny tidepool lab where paper shells mark story moments: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Draw a pretend map line through three lab moments, then write what changes between the first and last mark: ____________________.
cards.mapFrontPrompt: Map front: Place three paper shells on the lab map line for first, next, and finally; the first shell shows ____________________.
cards.mapBackPrompt: Map back: Add one small lab detail that changes after the middle shell, such as a jar, chart, clock face, or note: ____________________.
cards.storyShapePrompt: Story shape: The time map begins when ____________________, turns when ____________________, and ends when ____________________.
cards.firstLineBridge: First line bridge: Begin the story with the first tidepool lab moment and one clear clue: ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Check that the three moments happen in a clear order, then sharpen one time word: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Number the three shells silently before writing the middle moment here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Take this paper time map home and add one final tidepool lab sentence about ____________________.

cards.title: Revision River Ferry
cards.useCase: Adult-led, offline, paper-only printable story map card for moving a draft idea from fuzzy to clear across a fictional ferry page: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Print one card, fold a scrap page into two ferry docks, and label one side draft and one side clearer draft: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Write one draft sentence on the first dock, then use the ferry map line to carry a better version to the second dock: ____________________.
cards.mapFrontPrompt: Map front: The first ferry dock holds this draft sentence: ____________________.
cards.mapBackPrompt: Map back: The second ferry dock holds my clearer sentence with one stronger detail: ____________________.
cards.storyShapePrompt: Story shape: The revision map crosses from a plain idea to a clearer idea by changing ____________________.
cards.firstLineBridge: First line bridge: Start with the improved ferry sentence so the reader can picture ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Circle one vague word on the first dock and replace it with a concrete word on the second dock: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Work silently by copying only the clearer sentence onto the back dock: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Take this ferry revision map home and use it to polish one story sentence about ____________________.

cards.title: Clue Label Tower Museum
cards.useCase: Adult-led, offline, paper-only printable story map card for labeling invented museum clues so a quiet mystery scene feels clear: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Print one card, draw three blank label boxes, and remind the writer that every label belongs to a made-up exhibit: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Choose three invented exhibit clues, label each one, and connect the labels with a fictional map line: ____________________.
cards.mapFrontPrompt: Map front: The first tower museum label names an exhibit shaped like ____________________.
cards.mapBackPrompt: Map back: Add two more label clues, one for a texture and one for a sound: ____________________.
cards.storyShapePrompt: Story shape: The label map makes the story clearer because the first clue points to ____________________.
cards.firstLineBridge: First line bridge: Begin with the label that would make a reader lean closer: ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Replace one plain label with a sharper clue that names color, shape, texture, or sound: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Sketch one tiny label box first, then write its best clue here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Take this museum label map home and turn one clue into a first paragraph about ____________________.

cards.title: Compass Craft Academy
cards.useCase: Adult-led, offline, paper-only printable story map card for showing how one fictional academy choice changes a character's next step: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Print one card, draw a paper compass with four invented choice points, and ask the writer to pick two possible story moves: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Place a character at the center of the compass, choose one paper path, and explain why that choice matters: ____________________.
cards.mapFrontPrompt: Map front: The compass center shows a character who must choose between ____________________ and ____________________.
cards.mapBackPrompt: Map back: The chosen paper path leads to a new problem, helper, object, or question: ____________________.
cards.storyShapePrompt: Story shape: The choice map turns when the character decides ____________________ because ____________________.
cards.firstLineBridge: First line bridge: Start at the compass center with the moment before the choice: ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add one visible clue that proves the character made a clear choice: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Mark one compass point silently, then write the chosen story move here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Take this choice map home and write what happens after the academy compass points toward ____________________.

cards.title: Binding Day Boardwalk
cards.useCase: Adult-led, offline, paper-only printable story map card for putting boardwalk story pages into a clear beginning, middle, and ending order: ____________________.
cards.adultSetup: Print one card, cut or draw three paper page spots, and invite the writer to arrange a made-up boardwalk story: ____________________.
cards.kidDirection: Fill three page spots with story moments, then draw a map line that shows the order a reader should follow: ____________________.
cards.mapFrontPrompt: Map front: The first boardwalk page belongs at the start because it shows ____________________.
cards.mapBackPrompt: Map back: The middle page changes the story by adding ____________________, and the final page answers ____________________.
cards.storyShapePrompt: Story shape: The order map works when page one leads to ____________________, then the ending lands on ____________________.
cards.firstLineBridge: First line bridge: Begin with the boardwalk page that makes the next two moments make sense: ____________________.
cards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Move one page spot if the order feels jumpy, then write the bridge word or phrase that helps: ____________________.
cards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Number the three page spots silently, then copy the final order here: ____________________.
cards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Take this order map home and finish the boardwalk story with one clear ending sentence: ____________________.
